terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to take charge of, to manage, guide, administer … (the most usual signif. of this word; very freq. in Cic. and the histt.)”. Traupman gives it for managing on a large scale.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 4.13.7 (Lewis & Short): cūrāre omnia studiōsissimē ac dīligentissimē
terms.comment: Traupman’s first word for “manage”; see care, look after.

evidence: Cic. Att. 13.3.1: sī ipse negōtium meum gererem

terms.comment: The word of the steward (dispēnsātor) who keeps the household accounts.

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent; with an accusative or the dative
terms.comment: Classically to guide or govern, to keep within bounds (Lewis & Short); Traupman’s word for running a bank.

phrases.latin: quī sī ipse negōtium meum gererem, nihil gererem nisi cōnsiliō tuō
phrases.english: For if I were managing my business myself, I would do nothing without your advice.

phrases.latin: ex quō nihil scīre potuī dē nostrīs domesticīs rēbus. dē quibus acerbissimē adflīctor quod quī eās dispēnsāvit neque adest istīc neque ubi terrārum sit sciō
phrases.english: From it I could learn nothing about our household affairs; and they distress me bitterly, because the man who managed them is not there with you, and I do not know where in the world he is.
Who manages the household money? — Mum.

sources: Lewis & Short: administro · Lewis & Short: curo · Lewis & Short: gero · Lewis & Short: dispenso · Lewis & Short: moderor
